title: No command exposes a bundle's active type vocabulary; the unknown-type warning doesn't name valid types either
description:
User ask, verbatim, relayed via opum-agent 2026-09-18: "make sure the help / instructions are
fully reviewed and updated so that the actual agents know how to use the functionality properly."
That applies to whatever ships from this task -- see AC#2.

THE GAP, measured against dev at HEAD (75a783a9):

1. No command reads out a bundle's active type vocabulary (the profile's declared types, their
base + type-specific fields, and required sections). `lore help` lists 26 commands; none do this.
The closest is `lore schema export` (src/commands/schema.ts) -- but that WRITES
`.lore/schemas/*.schema.json` files to disk and requires the caller to already know a type name to
inspect usefully. It is a file-materialization command, not a discovery command. An agent that hits
an unknown-type warning has no CLI path to ask "what types does this bundle actually support" short
of hand-reading `.lore/schemas/*.json` plus `.lore/profile.toml` and reconciling the two -- exactly
what opum-agent's predecessor had to do by hand while investigating LCLI-534.

2. The unknown-type warning itself doesn't help either. src/core/schema.ts:315:
   options.warnings?.add(`unknown type "${type}"${where}; validated on \`type\` only`);
names only the rejected value, never the valid set. src/core/profile.ts:81's own comment claims the
profile's `case` setting "powers the unknown-type \"did you mean\" hint" -- but no hint is actually
emitted anywhere in the unknown-type path (schema.ts:315 is the only emission site); grepping the
source for "did you mean" turns up only that one comment. Either the hint was never wired up or was
removed and the comment never updated -- either way, documented behavior and actual behavior disagree.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: a read-only command (working name `lore types`) that prints the active
profile's type vocabulary -- names, base vs type-specific fields, required sections -- and fixing
the unknown-type warning to name the valid set and/or a nearest-match suggestion, closing the gap
profile.ts:81 already claims exists.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A command exists that prints a bundle's active type vocabulary (every declared type, its base and type-specific fields, and required sections) without the caller needing to already know a type name or hand-read .lore/schemas/*.json.
The unknown-type warning (src/core/schema.ts:315 today) names the valid type set, a nearest-match suggestion, or both -- it no longer reports only the rejected value.

lore instructions (and any topic it touches) and lore help / lore <command> --help for the new or changed commands are updated to describe the new behavior, so an agent driving lore learns about it from the tool itself.
bun run lint, typecheck and the test suite pass, and lore check exits 0.

plan: 1. Read core/profile.ts and core/schema.ts to find reusable per-type data (CompiledType.jsonSchema via schemaForVersion) without widening the Profile/CompiledType contract.
2. Add core/type-vocabulary.ts: buildTypeVocabulary + a generic Draft-7 shape reader (describeSchemaProperty), reusing schemaForVersion so a report matches what schema export writes to disk.

3. Wire commands/types.ts (lore types --type T) into core/manifest.ts, cli.ts COMMAND_HANDLERS, and core/agent-bridge.ts LORE_COMMANDS at the schema/scaffold registry position, keeping the manifest-router lockstep tests satisfied.

4. Fix the unknown-type warning at core/schema.ts around line 315: add unknownTypeHint, a known-type list plus Levenshtein did-you-mean, and correct the stale profile.ts comments claiming case powers a did-you-mean hint that was never wired.

5. Add a types instructions topic to core/instructions.ts, a types section in docs/reference/cli-surface.md, and a types.report row in cli-contract.md; fix the pre-existing stale instructions-topic list missing agents while touching that same line.
6. Update the golden exit-code and kind tables in test/help.test.ts, the one exact-message assertion in test/schema.test.ts, and add test/type-vocabulary.test.ts plus test/types.test.ts.
7. Run bun run lint, typecheck, the full test suite, lore check, and quest doctor; record the design-shape decisions as a task note; check off ACs and complete.
implementationNotes: DESIGN DECISION 1, output shape: added lore types --type T, kind types.report, seam profile only exit 0/2/6. For each declared type it reports name, slug, requiredSections, declared template, and a fields array where each field carries required, common, kind, and enum/itemKind when applicable. Field shape data is read from CompiledType.jsonSchema through schema.ts's schemaForVersion, exported for this purpose, rather than from a fresh copy of the profile FieldSpec grammar: this is the exact same Draft-7 JSON Schema schema export writes to .lore-schemas, so a types report can never disagree with what is on disk, and it also picks up the OKF 0.2 version-conditional families such as status and generated for free. A generic describeSchemaProperty reader turns a JSON Schema fragment into a short label such as string, list, datetime, enum, or a joined union like string or list, instead of a second hand-rolled kind mapping.

DESIGN DECISION 2, common vs type-specific classification: a field is common when its name appears in every declared type's effective field set post schemaForVersion, and type-specific otherwise; this is name-based, not TOML-table-based, so a type that overrides a base field by re-declaring the same name is still correctly common. Verified against the built-in profile: Story's own tasks and specs are non-common, the shared base fields and OKF 0.2 families such as status are common across every type, and Attested Computation's own runtime, parameters, computation, executor, and attester fields are non-common while its shared status/generated fields are common.

DESIGN DECISION 3, the unknown-type warning: chose to do both things the task offered as options rather than pick one. src/core/schema.ts's unknownTypeHint now appends known types: the full declared set, plus a did-you-mean suggestion from a plain case-insensitive Levenshtein match against those same names when the distance is within max of 2 and ceil of length over 3. Verified live: Stroy suggests Story, Glossary and Widget correctly get no suggestion. case-insensitive casing typos never reach this function at all, since canonicalType's byLowerName lookup already resolves those upstream in validateFrontmatter, so profile.ts's case setting genuinely cannot power a same-name-different-case suggestion; corrected two stale profile.ts comments that claimed otherwise, dated back before this task and never wired to anything.

SCOPE NOTE, a second unknown-type emission site left untouched: src/commands/check.ts around line 376 has its own separate unknown type message with the identical trailing wording validated on type only, used by lore check's scan-time unknown-type finding rather than validateFrontmatter's warning path. This task's AC named only src/core/schema.ts:315, so I left check.ts's literal as-is rather than widening scope, but the two now read inconsistently: validate names the valid set and check does not. Recorded as a cross-reference on LCLI-538, whose strict_types knob will likely touch this same check.ts site anyway.
finalSummary: Added lore types --type T (kind types.report), a read-only discovery command over the active profile's declared type vocabulary, sourced from the same Draft-7 JSON Schema lore schema export writes to disk (schemaForVersion, now exported) so the two can never disagree. Improved the unknown-type warning in core/schema.ts to name the full valid type set plus a Levenshtein did-you-mean suggestion, and corrected two stale profile.ts comments about a did-you-mean hint that was never wired. Wired the new command into the manifest, cli router, and agent-bridge command table; added a types instructions topic and cli-surface.md/cli-contract.md doc sections; added test/type-vocabulary.test.ts and test/types.test.ts, and updated help.test.ts/schema.test.ts/instructions.test.ts golden tables. Verified via bun run lint, typecheck, the full bun test suite (3249 pass, 0 fail), bun run src/cli.ts check (0 errors, 0 warnings), and quest doctor --json (healthy).
